statement: An international body gains inspection or compute-verification powers covering >= 2 of the top-5 compute jurisdictions (treaty text, official gazettes; by 2029-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met; no body has inspection or verification powers. 2026 produced only non-binding mechanisms: a UN scientific panel (assessment only) and global dialogue, and a Bloc A-Bloc B agreement to set up an AI-incident communication channel and dialogue (first session due November). Calls for an IAEA-style inspection agency came from Bloc A legislators and civil society, not governments.

items.summary: The UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI held its inaugural meeting; its mandate is evidence-based assessment, with no inspection or verification powers.
items.detail: Established by UNGA resolution A/RES/79/325 (2025-08-26); inaugural meeting UN HQ New York 2026-03-03. Preliminary report July 2026.

items.summary: The UN scientific panel published its preliminary report and the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance continued; both are deliberative fora without verification mandates.
items.detail: Preliminary Report PDF dated 2026-07 on un.org; Global Dialogue on AI Governance page. Exact day approximate.

items.summary: In high-level talks, Bloc A proposed a bilateral AI dialogue with a notification system for national-security-level AI incidents; chip export controls were excluded from the agenda.
items.detail: Bloc A Treasury Secretary Bessent and Vice Premier He Lifeng, New York talks ending 2026-09-20 (CNN, Al Jazeera).

items.summary: A Bloc A legislative committee held its first hearing calling for a binding, verifiable bilateral treaty on catastrophic AI risks, and a member urged the executive to work toward an IAEA-style international AI inspection agency with access to both blocs' data centres. Advocacy only.
items.detail: House Select Committee on the CCP (Democratic members) letter to Secretary of State Rubio following the hearing; date approximate (around the Sept 2026 Trump-Xi summit).

items.summary: After a leaders' summit, Bloc A and Bloc B agreed to set up a communication mechanism for AI-related incidents and an AI-specific dialogue scheduled for November - the first bilateral AI safety channel between the two largest compute jurisdictions, with no inspection or verification element. Bloc A's leader said separately it would not 'put on brakes'.
items.detail: Trump-Xi summit, Bloc A (AP via PBS; CNBC 2026-09-26). Guardian 2026-09-27 quotes Trump.

items.summary: No treaty text or gazette granting any international body inspection or compute-verification powers was found as of phase end; the first bilateral AI dialogue session was scheduled for November and had no published outcome.
items.detail: Checked UN mechanisms and Bloc A-Bloc B channel; Council of Europe Framework Convention has no compute verification. CNBC 2026-11-11 notes dialogue still pending.
